title: Universal injectivity is checked on source-algebra localizations
statement: Let R\to A be a homomorphism of commutative rings and u:M\to M\prime an A-linear map. For every q\in Spec(A) with p=q\cap R, let u_q:M_q\to M'_q be the localized map. Then u is universally injective over R (L\otimes _R u is injective for every R-module L) if and only if every u_q is universally injective over R_p. Localizations and spectra are [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and flatness is [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: We may use right tensor maps $u\otimes_R1_N$ in place of the left tensor maps in the statement. Indeed the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives the flip $n\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes n$, whose inverse is the reverse flip. On pure tensors it conjugates $1_N\otimes u$ to $u\otimes1_N$. The same argument applies over each $R_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Tag 05CL, lemma-universally-injective-check-stalks, proof of (1) equivalent to (4)

proof.text: Assume every $u_{\mathfrak q}$ is universally injective over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Fix any $R$-module $N$. Apply the local assumption to $N_{\mathfrak p}$ for each prime $\mathfrak q$ of $A$: every $u_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}1_{N_{\mathfrak p}}$ is injective. The fixed-test criterion [lem-trf-fixed-tensor-kernel-stalk-criterion] now gives injectivity of $u\otimes_R1_N$. Since $N$ was arbitrary, $u$ is universally injective over $R$.

source.place: Tag 05CL, lemma-universally-injective-check-stalks, proof of (1) equivalent to (4)

proof.text: Conversely suppose $u$ is universally injective over $R$, and denote the given ring map by $\varphi:R\to A$. Fix $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, and take any $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $L$. Restrict its scalars to $R$. Then $u\otimes_R1_L$ is injective; [lem-trf-fixed-tensor-kernel-stalk-criterion] gives injectivity of $T=u_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}1_{L_{\mathfrak p}}$. By the last clause of [lem-trf-contracted-prime-tensor-comparison], $j:L\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\mathfrak p}$, $l\mapsto l/1$, is an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-linear isomorphism. By the tensor universal property, $a=1_{M_{\mathfrak q}}\otimes j$ and $b=1_{M'_{\mathfrak q}}\otimes j$ have inverses $1_{M_{\mathfrak q}}\otimes j^{-1}$ and $1_{M'_{\mathfrak q}}\otimes j^{-1}$: each composite fixes every pure tensor, hence the whole tensor product. They satisfy $b\circ(u_{\mathfrak q}\otimes1_L)=T\circ a$: both send $m\otimes l$ to $u_{\mathfrak q}(m)\otimes(l/1)$. Explicitly, if $(u_{\mathfrak q}\otimes1_L)(z)=0$, the square gives $T(a(z))=0$; injectivity of $T$ gives $a(z)=0$, and invertibility of $a$ gives $z=0$. Since $L$ was arbitrary, $u_{\mathfrak q}$ is universally injective over $R_{\mathfrak p}$.
